core_step: Extract key frames from /root/super-mario.mp4 using ffmpeg and save as /root/keyframes_%03d.png
why_essential: Key frames are the input images on which grayscale conversion and object counting are performed; without extraction there are no frames to analyze.
evidence: ffmpeg -i /root/super-mario.mp4 -vf "select='eq(pict_type,I)'" -vsync vfr /root/keyframes_%03d.png ... The ffmpeg command extracted 4 key frames.

core_step: Verify that extracted keyframe files and template images exist by listing /root/keyframes_*.png and /root/enemy1.png /root/turtle1.png
why_essential: Confirming the presence of keyframes and template images ensures subsequent processing steps (grayscale conversion and template-based counting) can run successfully.
evidence: ls -la /root/keyframes_*.png ... and ls -la /root/enemy1.png /root/turtle1.png returned entries for /root/keyframes_001.png ... and the template files.

core_step: Convert each extracted keyframe in-place to grayscale using ImageMagick (convert ... -colorspace Gray)
why_essential: The task requires key frames to be converted to grayscale in-place before performing template-based object counting.
evidence: for f in /root/keyframes_001.png ...; do convert "$f" -colorspace Gray "$f"; done && echo "Done" ... Tool_result: "Done"

core_step: Run the object_counter tool to count enemies (using /root/enemy1.png) across the keyframes
why_essential: Counting enemies using the provided enemy template is required to produce the per-frame enemy counts for the CSV summary.
evidence: python3 .../count_objects.py --tool count ... --template /root/enemy1.png ... Output: "There are 0 objects (`/root/enemy1.png`) in file: `/root/keyframes_001.png`" (and results for other frames).

core_step: Run the object_counter tool to count turtles (using /root/turtle1.png) across the keyframes
why_essential: Counting turtles with the provided turtle template is required to produce the per-frame turtle counts for the CSV summary.
evidence: python3 .../count_objects.py --tool count ... --template /root/turtle1.png ... Output: "There are 0 objects (`/root/turtle1.png`) in file: `/root/keyframes_001.png`" and "There are 1 objects (`/root/turtle1.png`) in file: `/root/keyframes_002.png`"
